functions/consecutive-partition.md.history:
XPath 3.1 requires explicit recursion or stateful grouping logic to split at a boundary depending on the current partition. Grouping by route would merge nonadjacent orders, so it is not a semantics-preserving replacement for consecutive partitioning.

partition returns a sequence of arrays. Its split callback receives the current nonempty partition sequence, next item and one-based input position. A true result starts the next partition before that item. Empty input returns no partitions; a singleton returns one array and the callback is not invoked for its first item. The worked chapter combines capacity and route-change boundaries.

functions/higher-order-selection.md.history:
XPath 3.1 offers `some ... satisfies` and `every ... satisfies` quantified expressions. Positional `for` expressions can locate failures, as the linked baseline demonstrates. Function forms make the predicate a reusable function item; neither syntax nor callback contracts are interchangeable automatically.

some/every test whether any/all items satisfy a predicate; index-where returns one-based matching positions. The two-argument callbacks receive item and position. Empty predicate results mean false; arbitrary nonboolean callback results are errors. Empty input gives some=false, every=true and no positions. An explicit existence check is needed when an empty order is invalid.

[F&O 3.1 fn:compare](https://www.w3.org/TR/xpath-functions-31/#func-compare)
compares optional strings. The reviewed 4.0 draft expands the comparands to
optional atomic values. Numeric ordering compares their mathematical values
without the usual mixed-type promotion rounding; NaN orders below other numbers
and compares equal to NaN. This does not change the meaning of ordinary `eq` or
`lt` expressions. The earlier-version report below deliberately normalizes to
double and therefore gives a different boundary classification for row B.

all-different reports whether atomic values are pairwise distinct. duplicate-values reports each duplicated value once, in second-appearance order. operators-and-syntax/destructuring-let.m.history:
Supersedes three 3.1 idioms, one per container kind:

| Before (3.1) | After (4.0) |
|---|---|
| `let $x := $seq[1] let $y := $seq[2] return …` — repeated positional indexing, RHS re-evaluated per binding if not manually cached | `let $($x, $y) := $seq return …` — one evaluation, positional bind |
| `let $a := $arr(1) let $b := $arr(2) return …` | `let $[$a, $b] := $arr return …` |
| `let $n := map:get($m, "name") let $a := map:get($m, "addr") return …` | `let ${$name, $addr} := $m return …` — keys are the variable local names |

**Hexadecimal/binary integer literals and underscore separators** - **Frozen 4.0**, REQ-118 S3. Lowercase `0x` and `0b` introduce integer literals. Separators are permitted inside decimal, hexadecimal and binary digit groups, including the fraction and exponent groups of decimal/double literals. Ordinary XPath 3.0/3.1 syntax remains available; these extensions require 4.0.

Current comparison: [immutable grammar](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/b4723ff52fd9d4fabf2b4cd33bd44f21939c512c/specifications/grammar-40/xpath-grammar.xml), productions NumericLiteral, HexIntegerLiteral, BinaryIntegerLiteral, DecimalLiteral, DoubleLiteral, Digits, HexDigits and BinaryDigits. Upstream master was refreshed on 23 October 2026 at this revision. It is a current comparison pin, not a recovered historical adoption pin. [Delivery audit](../NUMERIC-LITERALS.md) separates the existing syntax from the source1.23.7 boundary correction; public release remains1.23.4.
operators-and-syntax/numeric-literals.md.history: In 3.1 use decimal `255` instead of `0xFF`, `4` instead of `0b0100`, and `1000` instead of `1_000`. operators-and-syntax/numeric-literals.md.implementation:
**C04 grammar review — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Expression/call/focus reconciliation](../EXPRESSION-CALL-FOCUS-RECONCILIATION.md) covers S3-lexical. Radix/separator token boundaries, template escaping/nesting/comment/atomization and old-profile/static-error cases are mapped. C03 retains numeric representation limits. Do not infer arbitrary precision, every adjacency/Unicode digit case, XML/XQuery string constructors or AVT/host behavior from these lexical probes. This is bounded production/profile evidence, not full grammar or AC-04 acceptance.


**C03 review — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Constructor/type reconciliation](../CONSTRUCTOR-TYPE-RECONCILIATION.md) verifies 4.0 radix/separator syntax and lower-profile refusal; Above-Int64 integer literals versus generic constructors/casts; Delivered floating thresholds, unsigned truncation and preserved integer identity. **Boundary:** A decimal-backed wide literal does not establish arbitrary precision or a matching generic constructor range. Generic wide xs:integer casts still narrow; .NET decimal precision remains bounded. Ownership: T01, T02. Per-path controls and named schema/API/host evidence are retained in the [review matrix](../CONSTRUCTOR-TYPE-RECONCILIATION.json); no whole-type or AC-04 acceptance follows.

Fifty new catalog cases use the existing public CatalogExampleTests execution path. Initial38 probes produced30 passes and8 failures: malformed fractional/exponent underscore groups were accepted. Source1.23.7 rejects those groups only in the 4.0 lexer path. Thirty-four dedicated API cases cover those eight shapes in all four compatibility levels and valid-group controls in both4.0 profiles. Expected outcomes were not weakened. [Audit and retained evidence](../NUMERIC-LITERALS.md).
